clue.text: Divides accommodation

definitions.meaning: splits into four equal parts, as a butcher does a carcass
lodgings, especially soldiers' or servants' rooms

explanation.surface: Someone splitting up living space between occupants.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means cuts into four; as a plural noun it means living quarters or lodgings.

clue.text: Queen comfortable, or nauseous?

parts.note: easy means relaxed or comfortable

explanation.surface: Asking whether the monarch is relaxed or feeling sick.
explanation.definitionFit: Queasy describes feeling sick in the stomach, the same as nauseous.

clue.text: Property that could be stripped

parts.note: refers to the business practice of buying a company and selling off its holdings piece by piece

explanation.surface: Suggests paint or wallpaper being stripped from a house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stripped' suggests peeling paint, but here it is the City practice of buying a firm and selling off its possessions piecemeal.
explanation.definitionFit: Valuable holdings of a company are what strippers sell off for a quick profit.

clue.text: He sits composing dissertation

indicators.note: composing means putting together, so the letters of he sits are rearranged

explanation.surface: A student settling down to write a dissertation.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesis is a long written treatise submitted for a university degree.

clue.text: Showing unwillingness, enact cruel change

definitions.note: a gerund phrase used as a noun, naming the state of being unwilling

indicators.note: change the letters of enact cruel into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone resisting a call to make a harsh law change.
explanation.definitionFit: Reluctance is hesitancy or disinclination to do something.

clue.text: Scrapes spades on parts of sleeve

parts.note: S is the card-suit abbreviation for spades
cuffs are the end parts of a sleeve at the wrist

explanation.surface: A card player's sleeves get worn by dragging over the table.
explanation.definitionFit: Scuffs and scrapes are both marks or abrasions made by rubbing against a surface.

clue.text: Mountain transport fitted with television?

parts.note: a car with cable TV read playfully as a gondola hauled up a cable

explanation.surface: A ski lift gondola with a TV screen inside.
explanation.walkthrough: Cable is both a hauling wire and a kind of television service.
explanation.definitionFit: A gondola hauled up a mountain along a wire, punningly a car with cable television.

clue.text: Even heavy metal is smoother

parts.note: flat means even or level
iron is a dense, heavy metal

explanation.surface: A claim that heavy metal music has a soothing effect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smoother' looks like a comparative adjective; it is a noun, a thing that smooths cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: An old iron heated on a stove, used to press creases out of clothes.

clue.text: Very surprised how one can be knocked

definitions.text: Very surprised how one can be knocked

parts.words: Very surprised how one can be knocked
parts.note: the idiom knocked for six or knocked off balance, here in its side-on form meaning astonished

explanation.surface: Astonishment at how easily someone can be hit.
explanation.definitionFit: To be knocked this way is a British idiom meaning thrown off balance by astonishment.

clue.text: Time for an egg? Extremely likely to give you wind

parts.note: Easter is the festival when chocolate eggs are given

indicators.note: the extremes of the word likely are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A jokey warning that eating Easter eggs will probably cause flatulence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' takes the outer letters LY of 'likely'. 'Wind' looks like flatulence in the surface, but it means a breeze.
explanation.definitionFit: An easterly is a breeze blowing from the east, used as a noun for that wind.

clue.text: Notice about pig on the train

indicators.note: the notice goes around the pig, so its letters are placed about the other piece

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement
a boar is a male pig

explanation.surface: A sign warning passengers that a pig is travelling on the train.
explanation.definitionFit: Aboard means carried on or in a vehicle, so it can replace riding on the train.

clue.text: Free kick routine producing some fireworks?

definitions.meaning: a rehearsed football move from a dead-ball situation
a fixed framework display of fireworks forming a picture

explanation.surface: A spectacular rehearsed free kick that brings the crowd to its feet.
explanation.definitionFit: In football it is a practised dead-ball move; in pyrotechnics it is a scaffold display of lights making a picture.

clue.text: Look again at magazine

definitions.meaning: a periodical, as in the title of many journals

explanation.surface: Someone rereading a periodical.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means reconsider or reassess; as a noun it is a periodical publication, as in many journal titles.

clue.text: Failing to give penny to man somehow?

indicators.note: somehow means in some way or other, so the letters of penny to man are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone stingily not handing a coin to a beggar.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonpayment is the failure to hand over money owed.

clue.text: Trials here to get dog speaking?

parts.note: lab is short for Labrador, a breed of dog
oratory is the art of public speaking

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about whether experiments could make a dog talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speaking' looks like a homophone signal, but it supplies a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A laboratory is the place where experiments and tests are carried out.

clue.text: As cover for wound, pick up dull-coloured sheath

parts.note: a scab forms over a healing wound

indicators.note: in a down clue, picking up lifts the word for dull-coloured so it reads from the bottom

parts.note: drab means dull or dreary in colour

explanation.surface: Choosing a dull-coloured covering to bandage an injury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pick up' reverses DRAB to BARD in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A scabbard is the case or sheath that holds a sword or dagger.

clue.text: Minor thoroughfares with a lot of theatres

definitions.text: Minor thoroughfares with a lot of theatres

parts.note: B as in a B-road, a minor road in Britain
a roadway is a thoroughfare

explanation.surface: Side streets lined with many playhouses.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, B-roads are minor roads, below A-roads.
explanation.definitionFit: The New York avenue famous as the heart of American theatre.

clue.text: Said to have cut exam for this kind of 3?

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the following words are heard rather than read

parts.note: to doctor an animal is to neuter or cut it; an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A rumour about cutting short an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 3 is the answer to 3 down, a dissertation; a doctoral one is written for a PhD.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to a doctorate, the level of degree for which such a dissertation is written.

clue.text: One was impressed by an old typewriter

definitions.text: One was impressed by an old typewriter

parts.words: One was impressed by an old typewriter
parts.note: the duplicate sheet under the top page received the struck letters through carbon paper

explanation.surface: Someone admiring a vintage writing machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Impressed' means awed in the surface but physically pressed here: the key strikes printed through onto a second sheet.
explanation.definitionFit: A duplicate made with carbon paper under the top sheet records each keystroke pressed onto it.

clue.text: Bob twice gets this old piece of silver

definitions.text: Bob twice gets this old piece of silver

parts.words: Bob twice gets this old piece of silver
parts.note: two bob, two shillings, was the value of a pre-decimal British coin

explanation.surface: A man named Bob being paid twice in silver coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a name but is British slang for a shilling; the two-shilling coin was this.
explanation.definitionFit: A British two-shilling coin from before decimalisation, originally minted in silver.

clue.text: Feeble, but employed by business

parts.note: someone employed by a company works in it
a firm is a business

explanation.surface: A weak worker who still holds down a job.
explanation.definitionFit: Infirm means physically weak, especially through age or illness.

clue.text: Persist as Welsh symbol

definitions.meaning: the red beast on the flag of Wales

explanation.surface: Wales keeping its national emblem.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means to go on too long; whole, it is the mythical creature on the Welsh flag.

clue.text: Bravo — survives gales

parts.note: B is Bravo in the NATO phonetic alphabet
lasts means endures or survives

explanation.surface: A cheer for something that withstands storms.
explanation.definitionFit: Blasts are strong gusts of wind, so they can stand for gales.

clue.text: It is appealingly drawn on the lid

definitions.text: It is appealingly drawn on the lid

parts.words: It is appealingly drawn on the lid
parts.note: make-up pencilled along the eyelid to attract

explanation.surface: Something attractively sketched on a box or jar top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lid' suggests a container's top, but it is the eyelid.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmetic applied as a line along the edge of the eyelid to make the eyes attractive.

clue.text: In lifeboat, couple busy

indicators.note: the couple is placed in the lifeboat, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: Noah's ark served as the lifeboat in the Flood
a couple is two

explanation.surface: A pair of crew members busy on a lifeboat.
explanation.walkthrough: The ark took animals in by twos, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at work means occupied with a job, so the phrase means busy.

clue.text: Finding out alternative to large inn

indicators.note: an alternative arrangement of the words large inn reshuffles their letters

explanation.surface: A traveller discovering another place to stay besides a big hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: Learning is acquiring knowledge, discovering facts one did not know.

clue.text: Not born yesterday? On the contrary

definitions.text: Not born yesterday? On the contrary

parts.words: Not born yesterday? On the contrary
parts.note: the phrase for not naive is reversed into a literal description of something only one day into life

explanation.surface: Someone insisting they are no fool, then contradicting themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'not born yesterday' means shrewd; on the contrary, a chick that hatched yesterday is literally born yesterday.
explanation.definitionFit: A creature only one day into life, such as a newly hatched chick, was literally born yesterday.

clue.text: Make chap smaller, or double

definitions.meaning: read as a verb phrase: stunt (check growth) a man (chap)
a performer standing in for an actor in dangerous scenes

explanation.surface: A choice between shrinking a man or doubling him.
explanation.definitionFit: A film double performs dangerous action scenes in place of a star; read as two words it means to stunt a chap's growth.
